simple.meaning: פֶּתַע (pethaʻ) is a Hebrew word meaning “a wink , i.e. moment (used only [with or without preposition] adverbially, quickly or unexpectedly ).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: פֶּתַע (H6621) appears 7 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Numbers 6:9, with occurrences in Numbers, Proverbs, Isaiah, Habakkuk.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פֶּתַע (H6621) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in פֶּתַע (H6621) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: פֶּתַע (pethaʻ) / H6621 is traced through Numbers 6:9, Numbers 35:22, Proverbs 6:15, Proverbs 29:1 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: a wink , i.e. moment (used only [with or without preposition] adverbially, quickly or unexpectedly )
definitions.full: H6621. petha מֶּתַע substantive suddenness ( √ unknown: compare Assyrian ina pitti, ina pittimma , in suddenness , instantly , Dl HWB 553 ): — Num 35:22 . . . וְאִםבְּֿפֶתַע הֲדָפוֺ if he have thrust him in suddenness , before he is aware what he has done (i.e. accidentally); + מִּתְאֹם 6:9 פתאם בפתע עליו מת ימות וכי i.e. very suddenly; לְפֶתַע according to ( לְ , p. 5 I 6 b) suddenness , Isa 29:5 פתאם לפתע והיה = at an instant , suddenly, 30:13 יבוא לפתע פתאם אשׁר שִׁבְרָהּ . As adverb accusative, suddenly , Prov 6:15 (= 29:1 ) יִשָּׁבֵר מֶּתַע , Hab 2:7 .
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to open (the eyes); (compare 6597 )

occurrences.englishText: “ ‘If any man dies very suddenly beside him, and he defiles the head of his separation, then he shall shave his head in the day of his cleansing. On the seventh day he shall shave it.
“ ‘But if he shoved him suddenly without hostility, or hurled on him anything without lying in wait,
Therefore his calamity will come suddenly.
He who is often rebuked and stiffens his neck
But the multitude of your foes will be like fine dust, and the multitude of the ruthless ones like chaff that blows away. Yes, it will be in an instant, suddenly.
therefore this iniquity shall be to you like a breach ready to fall, swelling out in a high wall, whose breaking comes suddenly in an instant.
Won’t your debtors rise up suddenly, and wake up those who make you tremble, and you will be their victim?
